newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares higher in year's last bourse session.
newsitem.headline: German shares higher in year's last bourse session.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index of blue-chip shares opened the last day's trade of the year around three-quarters of a percent higher as the bull market continued to prevail and the stronger dollar lifted the market.
The index came off a little as the session went on and by 1004 GMT the DAX stood at 2,868.52 points, up 15.64 points or 0.55 percent.

Electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index was due to end at 1300 GMT before the New Year holiday, reopening again on Thursday. Dealers said that some of their colleagues did not make it into work because of heavy snow in Germany.

"This is real end of the year stuff, turnover is thin and everyone is trying to keep clean books. We're also closing early, which won't help volumes, and a lot of people didn't make it because of the snow," said one Frankfurt broker.
The strong dollar helped underpin the market early on. The U.S. currency stood at 1.5542 marks, slightly off earlier levels but still strong enough to boost exporting stocks.
Among the big winners in early trade was industrial giant Daimler Benz AG, up 1.95 marks at 105.60 marks.
Reinsurance group Munich Re was down 10 marks at 3,755 marks in early bourse trade, having traded 1.20 percent higher in electronic IBIS trade.
Dealers said that prices reflected year-end activity, such as short-covering, rather than any fundamental issues.
